mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or equivalent business registration certificate of the foreign sole shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent competent authority in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel path (never sequential): (1) Hague Apostille: notarization by a local notary where required, then issuance of an apostille certificate by the designated competent authority of the country of origin, then certified Chinese translation. (2) Consular Legalization: only for non-members of the Apostille Convention; notarization, then legalization by the foreign ministry of the country of origin, then legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in that country, then certified Chinese translation. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Status of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or corporate registrar of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel path (never sequential): (1) Hague Apostille: notarization as required, apostille by the competent authority in the country of origin, then certified Chinese translation. (2) Consular Legalization: only for non-Apostille states; notarization, foreign ministry legalization, Chinese Embassy/Consulate legalization, then certified Chinese translation. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing formation of the WFOE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign shareholder (certified by corporate secretary or notary)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel path (never sequential): (1) Hague Apostille: notarization/certification of signatory capacity, apostille by the competent authority in the jurisdiction of issuance, then certified Chinese translation. (2) Consular Legalization: only for non-Apostille Convention states; notarization, ministry legalization, Chinese Embassy/Consulate legalization, then certified Chinese translation. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum and Articles or constitutional documents of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or authorized corporate service provider in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel path (never sequential): (1) Hague Apostille: notarization of certified copy, apostille by competent authority, then certified Chinese translation. (2) Consular Legalization: only for non-members; notarization, foreign ministry legalization, Chinese Embassy/Consulate legalization, then certified Chinese translation. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter / Creditworthiness letter for the foreign shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel path (never sequential): (1) Hague Apostille: bank officer signature notarized, apostille by competent authority in the bank's jurisdiction, then certified Chinese translation. (2) Consular Legalization: only for non-Apostille states; notarization, foreign ministry legalization, Chinese Embassy/Consulate legalization, then certified Chinese translation. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories must be screened before any filing against: (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists; (iii) the Chinese domestic sanctions/designation lists administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the People's Bank of China; (iv) global PEP databases covering executive, legislative, judicial, and military officials, as well as senior state-owned enterprise appointments; (v) adverse media and integrity watchlists such as World-Check. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, connection to a high-risk jurisdiction, or complex multi-layer ownership. Screening results must be documented, risk-rated, and escalated to the AML compliance officer before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Self-Declaration System through the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name must be in simplified Chinese characters. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) administrative division (e.g., Shanghai, Beijing); (2) unique trade name or brand; (3) industry characteristic matching the declared business scope (e.g., digital publishing, information technology); and (4) legal form (Limited Liability Company). Foreign brand names must be transliterated into Chinese phonetically or as a licensed Chinese translation; an English name may be registered for customs and banking convenience but cannot replace the Chinese legal name. Pinyin is accepted only when the trade name is a proper noun or registered trademark transliteration. Latin letters, Arabic numerals, and other symbols are prohibited unless expressly permitted by the enterprise name registration rules.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the SAMR enterprise name system rejects the proposed name, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the local market regulation bureau within 15 days, attaching the rejection notice, the four-tier name structure, trademark or brand evidence, and a written explanation of distinctiveness. If the local bureau upholds the rejection, the applicant may apply for administrative reconsideration with the next higher SAMR authority within 60 days, or bring an administrative lawsuit under the Administrative Litigation Law within six months. The appeal must specify the legal basis under the Measures for the Registration and Administration of Enterprise Names and identify the conflicting registry entry or policy ground.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox-only address is not permissible as the sole registered office for a WFOE in China. The local SAMR, tax authority, and public security bureau require a fixed physical business premises evidenced by a valid lease agreement and landlord property ownership certificate or authorization. Banks invariably conduct a physical due-diligence visit before opening the corporate account and will reject a postal-only address lacking company signage, office equipment, and personnel. For an ISIC 5820 digital game publisher, a serviced office with a dedicated desk and access to landlord property documentation may be acceptable, but it is functionally a physical office and must support the statutory inspection standard.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 30% probability of an unannounced physical inspection during the first 12 months after WFOE incorporation, given SAMR and municipal tax bureau random-inspection quotas. Checklist for inspection readiness: (i) company name plate/signage visible at the registered address; (ii) original lease agreement and property ownership certificate; (iii) business license available on site; (iv) office furniture and IT equipment consistent with the declared business; (v) employees present or payroll records available; (vi) accounting books, VAT invoices, and bank statements; (vii) no mail-forwarding-only arrangement; (viii) where applicable, network security filing under the Multi-Level Protection Scheme. Failure of an unannounced inspection may result in administrative penalty, deregistration, or tax registration cancellation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), effective 1 July 2024, Articles 23 to 37 on formation of limited liability companies, Article 47 on the five-year capital contribution period, and Articles 59 to 67 on corporate governance; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 4, 6, 7 and 30; Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (State Council Order No. 746), Articles 2 to 14.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), Enterprise Registration Bureau, through the local Municipal Market Regulation Bureau having delegated registration authority over foreign-invested companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company filed on the SAMR National Integrated Online Government Service Platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The PRC Company Law and Foreign Investment Law do not impose a statutory minimum registered capital for a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company in the digital software publishing sector (ISIC 5820). Registered capital is subscribed as stated in the Articles of Association, and each shareholder must pay the subscribed contribution in full within five years from incorporation unless a shorter period is specified in the articles. No blocked escrow account is required by national law; capital contributions must be remitted into the company's foreign exchange capital account through approved banking channels and reported under the SAFE direct investment framework.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [CN_WFOE_LTD] (the 'Company')

A meeting of the board of directors of the Company was duly convened and held on [date] at [registered office]. All directors were present, a quorum was satisfied, and the meeting was regularly held in accordance with the Articles of Association and applicable law.

WHEREAS the Company is being formed as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise limited liability company under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China; and

WHEREAS the board must establish the corporate, banking and administrative architecture required for the registration and continuing operation of the Company.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED UNANIMOUSLY AS FOLLOWS:

1. AUTHORIZATION OF SHARE CAPITAL. The authorized share capital of the Company shall be the amount stated in the Articles of Association, divided into ordinary shares. The sole shareholder shall subscribe for all issued shares, and the subscription monies shall be paid into the Company's capital contribution account in compliance with the Articles of Association and the foreign exchange control rules. The legal representative is authorized to issue share certificates and to record all transfers.

2. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. [Name] is appointed executive director and legal representative; [Name] is appointed general manager; and [Name] is appointed supervisor. Each appointee accepts office and undertakes to exercise powers in accordance with the Company Law and the Articles of Association.

3. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office located at [address] is adopted as the statutory seat forthwith. Management is empowered to execute and perform the lease, pay deposits and rents, and maintain the office as the registered address.

4. DESIGNATION OF BANKING AUTHORITIES. [Bank name and branch] is designated as the principal banker. The legal representative, general manager and chief financial officer are authorized, by any two acting together, to open bank accounts, determine authorized signatories, execute facility documents and receive proceeds from Steam Valve, PlayStation Store and other digital distribution platforms.

5. FILINGS AND REGISTRATIONS. Management is authorized to prepare and submit applications to the State Administration for Market Regulation, the tax authorities, the social insurance authorities, the Ministry of Commerce and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, and to obtain all corporate seals.

6. RATIFICATION. All acts done and documents signed before this resolution are ratified and confirmed.

This resolution is effective upon adoption and shall be recorded in the corporate minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Name Reservation and Market Entity Registration Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Online Platform / local Municipal Market Regulation Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign investor must prepare the investment plan, draft the Articles of Association, and secure a valid commercial lease for the registered office. The company name is reserved through the SAMR online registration portal or the local Market Regulation Bureau window using the format 'territory + trade name + industry characteristics + limited company'. The foreign investor's certificate of incorporation and good standing must receive an Apostille under the Hague Convention or, where appropriate, consular legalization, and all documents must be translated into Chinese by a qualified translator. After name reservation is granted, submit the market entity registration application electronically, attaching the Articles of Association, office lease, landlord ownership certificate, and identity documents of the legal representative, directors and supervisor. The registry will review the application against the Foreign Investment Negative List and issue the business license.
required_dossiers: Apostilled or legalized certificate of incorporation and good standing of the foreign shareholder
Chinese translation of all foreign investor corporate documents
Draft Articles of Association and signed consent of directors and supervisor
Name reservation approval notice
Lease agreement for registered office and landlord property ownership certificate
Identification documents of the legal representative, directors and supervisor
Power of attorney if a filing agent is engaged
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR returns the application for correction, the applicant has 10 working days to rectify and re-submit. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may re-file with a new name. If the registration is refused, the applicant may request a hearing before the registry, and may then apply for administrative reconsideration within 60 days or institute administrative litigation within 6 months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution and Banking / SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated commercial bank with foreign exchange licence and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) local branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the business license, the legal representative or a person authorized by board resolution must attend the designated bank to open a capital contribution foreign exchange account and a basic settlement deposit account. The bank will require the company's unified social credit code, business license, Articles of Association, First Board Resolution, company seal, and original identity documents of signatories. For an inbound capital contribution, the company must complete the foreign-investment information report with MOFCOM and satisfy the SAFE foreign direct investment foreign-exchange registration through the bank's direct investment system before remitting funds. Once the remittance is received, the bank records the capital contribution, and the finance department confirms paid-in capital in the statutory books. Any change in contribution schedule, currency or shareholder requires a supplementary board resolution and filing.
required_dossiers: Original business license and unified social credit code
Articles of Association and First Board Resolution
Foreign direct investment foreign exchange registration form or bank-generated FDI code
Company seal, financial seal and legal representative seal
Identity documents of all authorized signatories
Source-of-funds documents for inbound capital remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or SAFE raises a query, the company must promptly provide additional evidence of beneficial ownership and source of funds. If a capital remittance is blocked, the company must cooperate with the bank's compliance review. If the bank refuses the transaction, the applicant may escalate the matter to the local SAFE branch, correct the foreign-exchange information report and re-file; administrative and judicial remedies remain available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Social Insurance and Statistics Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Tax Service Bureau of the State Taxation Administration, local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau, and local Statistics Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within thirty days after receiving the business license, the company must complete tax registration at the local tax service hall or through the electronic tax bureau, obtain a taxpayer identification number, enroll employees in social insurance and housing fund schemes, and register with the national market entity statistics system. The financial officer must establish accounting records in accordance with Chinese Accounting Standards and complete bank account information filing with the tax authority. The company must determine whether it qualifies as a small-scale taxpayer or a general taxpayer for value-added tax purposes and make any required stamp-duty filings. The legal representative or authorized personnel should also apply for electronic invoicing capability. These post-incorporation filings are mandatory and must be maintained continuously.
required_dossiers: Business license and unified social credit code
Tax registration application form
Legal representative identification document
Office lease and landlord title certificate
Articles of Association and First Board Resolution
Social insurance enrollment form and employee information list
Bank account opening certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any tax, social insurance or statistics registration fails, the competent authority issues a deficiency notice; the company must correct the submission within the specified grace period, ordinarily 10 working days. Where the authority alleges dual registration or incomplete information, the company should submit a formal written explanation and supporting documents. Statutory rights of administrative reconsideration and administrative litigation apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Records, Seal Engraving and Legal Representative Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR local enterprise registration office for record-filing and local Public Security Bureau for seal engraving authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The board must hold a formal meeting or sign a unanimous written resolution to approve the adoption of internal governance rules, issue shares, confirm the appointment of statutory officers, and authorize banking signatories. The First Board Resolution and minutes must be placed in the corporate minute book. The company must then apply to the local Public Security Bureau for seal-engraving permits and arrange for a licensed engraving house to produce the company seal, financial seal, contract seal and legal representative seal. All seal specifications must be registered and receipts retained. In parallel, the company must maintain the register of members, minutes book and paid-in capital records. Any later amendment to the Articles of Association or change of legal representative must be filed with SAMR within thirty days.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution and signed minutes
Articles of Association
Business license and unified social credit code
Identification documents of directors, supervisor and legal representative
Seal engraving permit application to Public Security Bureau
Consent letters of statutory officers
Register of members and share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR or the Public Security Bureau rejects a filing or seal permit, the company should verify the authenticity of the registered office lease and identity documents, correct any inconsistency (including amending the Articles of Association if necessary), and re-file. A formal refusal may be challenged through administrative reconsideration within 60 days or administrative litigation within 6 months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the entity is not engaged in ISIC 1xxx, 2xxx, 3xxx, 4xxx or 52xx physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing activities; ISIC 5820 digital software publishing does not trigger industrial licensing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China - Not Applicable to this entity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable - no construction project, industrial plant, chemical operation or physical facility requiring Environmental Impact Assessment filing or environmental registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater, VOC, dust, noise or hazardous waste streams are generated by a digital-only software publishing office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable to industrial civil-defense or fire clearance requirements. The office tenant must nevertheless comply with the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China by maintaining portable fire extinguishers, ensuring unobstructed egress, and retaining the building's fire-safety inspection certificate. No civil-defense construction permit, hazardous-occupation approval, or industrial fire permit is required for a digital-only software publishing operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, administered through the National Unified Electronic Tax Service Platform (the Electronic Tax Bureau online portal).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: The non-resident investor incorporates the WFOE with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); the consolidated business license carries the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the WFOE's statutory PRC Tax Identification Number. Step 2: Within 30 days of license issuance, the WFOE must complete tax registration and taxpayer information confirmation through the Electronic Tax Bureau, declaring its legal representative, registered address, business scope, bank settlement account, accounting policies, capital structure, and anticipated taxable activities. Step 3: The competent tax authority opens the taxpayer file, confirms the VAT taxpayer classification (general or small-scale), and grants electronic invoicing privileges through the Digital Electronic Invoice Service Platform. Step 4: If physical exports are made, the WFOE must register with the China Customs Single Window and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) trade monitoring system through a designated foreign exchange bank so that export receipts can be collected and repatriated under PRC trade procedures. Step 5: A foreign non-resident shareholder without a Chinese establishment does not receive a separate PRC VAT ID; the WFOE is the resident taxpayer and acts as withholding agent for China-source payments, reporting the foreign entity's name, country of tax residence, and foreign tax identifier in the required withholding returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: For corporate income tax, PRC law provides no check-the-box election, fiscal unity election, or hybrid mismatch election; the WFOE is necessarily a separate entity-level taxpayer. For VAT, the available statutory election is between small-scale taxpayer treatment (applicable while annual taxable sales remain below RMB 5,000,000) and general VAT taxpayer treatment; general status is mandatory once annual taxable sales reach RMB 5,000,000, and may be voluntarily selected if the entity maintains proper accounting records. No pass-through or tax-transparent election exists for this limited liability WFOE.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (China Value-Added Tax) under the unified PRC VAT system; the headline statutory rate for taxable goods is 13%, general taxable services are 6%, and qualifying cross-border exported goods or digital services are zero-rated or exempt under the STA's cross-border tax rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable sales; this is the mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration threshold. Tax registration using the Unified Social Credit Code is compulsory upon incorporation, so the turnover threshold governs the compulsory conversion from small-scale taxpayer status to general VAT taxpayer status rather than the initial existence of a VAT registration obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates the Golden Tax Phase IV digital fiscal-control and invoice-clearance framework. General VAT taxpayers must issue fully digitalized electronic invoices through the STA's Digital Electronic Invoice Service Platform; every invoice is transmitted to the tax authority in near-real time and carries a uniform tax-control code, encrypted electronic seal, and digital signature produced by STA-approved credentials. The system performs automatic invoice matching, red/blue invoice reconciliation, and risk-based blocking of suspicious issuances; high-volume taxpayers may connect system-to-system via an API gateway, while all other taxpayers use the state portal. No private paper tax stamps are permitted, and issuers must obtain an electronic invoice allocation from the tax authority before issuing any taxable invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For physical goods, 0% VAT (export zero-rating and export-tax refund) applies where the goods are lawfully exported from the PRC customs territory, title and risk pass to a non-resident purchaser, the goods are not consumed in China, and the exporter can produce customs clearance records and bank-verified foreign exchange receipts. For digital game publishing and offshore services, zero-rating or VAT exemption is available only where the service or software right is supplied to a non-resident recipient, the recipient is located outside China, the service is wholly consumed outside China, and the foreign consideration is received from outside China. The WFOE must demonstrate that Steam/PlayStation sales are offshore supplies and not downloads by PRC domestic users; if digital services are partly used in China, only the offshore portion qualifies. The claim requires a cross-border contract, a platform settlement/payout report, bank receipts evidencing foreign currency inflow, and a non-resident tax/residency certificate from the overseas platform operator; zero-rating is never automatic.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration made through the China International Trade Single Window evidencing physical export clearance and the exporter-of-record status
Bill of Lading, airway bill, or equivalent international transport document proving the goods left the PRC customs territory
Commercial invoice, packing list, and export contract/purchase order
Bank-issued export proceeds receipt and SAFE Cross-Border Receipts and Payments Declaration data evidencing repatriation of foreign currency to China
Cross-border service/publishing agreement, Steam or PlayStation Store platform settlement statement, and non-resident recipient tax residency certificate for digital/offshore service exports
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and SAFE cross-match customs declarations, VAT invoices, service contracts, platform payout records, and bank FX receipts through the Golden Tax IV risk-control system. If the supporting documentation is incomplete, inconsistent, backdated, or contradicted by invoice/platform data, the zero-rating is denied and the supply is recharacterized as a domestic taxable supply; the WFOE must immediately pay the applicable output VAT, file amended returns, and pay a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% on the overdue tax. Under Article 63 of the PRC Law on the Administration of Tax Levying and Collection, successful tax evasion or false zero-rating claims trigger a penalty of 50% to five times the tax involved and full clawback of any refunded amount. Serious cases are referred under Article 204 of the Criminal Law for fraudulent export tax refund, which may result in imprisonment, fines, or life imprisonment for extremely large fraud; exporters also face downgrade in the STA export-tax-refund classification, cancellation of electronic invoice quota, customs penalties for false declarations, and public credit blacklisting.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) as the central bank, with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) as the delegated foreign-exchange regulator and licensing authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains current-account convertibility under a managed floating exchange-rate regime, but the capital account remains tightly controlled. The WFOE may receive Steam/PlayStation digital publishing revenue as current-account service income after bank verification of genuine contracts, invoices, and platform payout statements, and may hold or convert such foreign currency at domestic banks at the prevailing market rate. Registered capital injections and any financing between the foreign parent and WFOE are capital-account transactions and require SAFE registration/FDI reporting, a dedicated foreign-exchange capital account, and usage restrictions under the FDI no-negative-list and positive-use rules. Profit remittance is possible only after annual statutory audit, payment of 25% Chinese corporate income tax, withholding tax on dividend distributions, and bank review of audited financial statements, board resolution, tax clearance, and SAFE payment verification; the remittance amount cannot exceed after-tax distributable profits. There is no blanket foreign-exchange surrender requirement, but all cross-border receipts must be repatriated into a licensed domestic bank account before conversion. Full RMB free convertibility outside the current account is not available.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under current SAFE rules there is no fixed compulsory surrender ratio or mandatory conversion percentage for export receipts. Goods-export proceeds must be brought back into China and settled through the trade-foreign-exchange monitoring system, generally within 90 days of the export customs declaration unless an extension is approved. For the WFOE's digital publishing revenue from Valve Steam and PlayStation Store, the receipts are classified as cross-border services/electronic-license income; the WFOE must present the platform agreements, royalty statements, and invoices to the settlement bank, and proceeds must be deposited into the domestic current-account foreign-currency collection account. The WFOE may elect to retain the FX balance or convert the receipts to CNY at the onshore market rate, subject to verification of the underlying commercial transaction.

Basic Operational Currency Account; Foreign Exchange Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs have low viability in China mainland. They are not licensed by PBOC or SAFE to operate corporate RMB accounts, conduct SAFE FX verification, hold registered capital, or remit dividends from a WFOE, and a WFOE may not lawfully rely on them for primary treasury operations. P2P-style virtual-account aggregators or foreign EMI cards can only be auxiliary collection tools for overseas consumer receipts outside China; they cannot clear offshore Steam/PlayStation payouts into the WFOE's regulated banking perimeter or substitute for a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank. Any entity promising EMI-based settlement into a WFOE would create unlicensed payment activity under PRC regulations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, Chinese Tier-1 banks require the WFOE's statutory representative/legal representative to appear physically in a mainland branch to execute the RMB basic-deposit-account application, grant bank-signature authority, and complete the AML interview. Remote consular proxy account opening is not accepted for formal corporate accounts; only after the legal representative is KYC-cleared may a delegated finance officer be nominated as the daily account operator. Foreign shareholders must provide notarized and legalized corporate documents, the WFOE business license, FDI/SAFE registration form, articles of association, and valid passports; the bank retains the right to perform video/on-site verification where the shareholding chain is complex.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO opacity: the parent and ultimate shareholder are outside mainland China, and the exact human beneficial ownership cannot be traced because of intermediate holding structures or bearer share history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate registry extracts and register of members from each intermediate jurisdiction; UBO declaration or registry certificate; group organizational chart stamped by the parent; certified passports of all natural persons owning 10% or more; source-of-wealth statement with supporting audited financial statements; senior-management identification; notarized English/Chinese translations of all offshore company documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered capital injection is sourced from a related foreign entity whose operating income does not clearly map to the declared capital subscription, creating suspicion of round-tripping or unlicensed cross-border financing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed share-subscription/equity transfer agreement; board and shareholder resolutions approving the WFOE capital outlay and payment schedule; bank SWIFT MT103 remittance history of the funding entity; audited annual reports and bank statements of the remitter for the previous 2 years; tax payment records explaining the accumulated retained earnings; legal opinion confirming the offshore parent's solvency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital video-game revenue from Steam/PlayStation is hard to substantiate under banking documentary standards because the sales are remote, download-based, and involve high transaction volumes with consumers but no physical customs declaration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed publisher/license agreements with Valve Corporation and Sony Interactive Entertainment; monthly sales/royalty reconciliation reports from Steamworks and PSN/PlayStation Partner Portal; game-title software copyright registration certificates; invoices/payment advices; platform territorial availability evidence; export-sales ledger and product release documentation; geoblocking/territory-restriction compliance documentation excluding sanctioned jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound royalty or dividend payments to offshore affiliates may breach transfer-pricing taxation or conceal controlled-foreign-company structures; bank requires proof that the payment is commercially genuine and tax-cleared.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Royalty or profit-split agreements between WFOE and each overseas affiliate; transfer pricing documentation / BEPS-aligned local-file summary for the software license; corporate income tax prepayment returns and proof of withholding tax (EIT on profits and dividend WHT) paid to the State Taxation Administration; tax clearance certificates; board minutes declaring distributable profits; SAFE service-trade payment application forms and purpose codes; annual audit report and legalization certificates for overseas recipient.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All registered-capital injections must be wired by SWIFT MT103 from the foreign parent to the WFOE's designated domestic-bank Foreign Exchange Capital Account. Before dispatch, the WFOE must complete FDI status/SAFE registration with the branch bank and obtain the FDI identification number; remittance instructions must include the creditor/shareholder name and clearly state the purpose as foreign-invested enterprise equity capital injection with the applicable SAFE capital-project transaction code. Upon credit, the domestic bank records the receipt in the Foreign Exchange Capital Project Information System, and a PRC-registered certified public accountant issues a capital-verification report. The WFOE may then convert the capital or use it only for business-scope operations; capital cannot be diverted into securities, entrusted loans, RMB settlement of foreign debt, or non-business real estate unless in the permitted positive list.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For ordinary licensing/royalty payments to overseas developers or platform-related service providers, the WFOE should use SWIFT MT103 with the underlying publisher agreement, proforma/invoice, withholding tax vouchers, and SAFE service-trade payment form. For high-value consignments of physical media, console accessories, or collector's editions, a commercial letter of credit (MT700/MT103 matching) issued by the domestic bank through its corresponding-beneficiary bank is available under Incoterms, with transport bills and inspectable shipping documents. Documentary collections (D/P or D/A) are viable only for trusted repetitive trade counterparties and require complete shipping set plus bank acknowledgment. All outbound payments require sanctions/PEP screening of the beneficiary bank, SWIFT BIC validation, and a stable OFAC/UN-EU sanctions exclusion statement from the WFOE.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts between CNY and USD/EUR/JPY/GBP, executed with licensed domestic banks against a verified current-account revenue or expense exposure, ordinarily requiring no speculative open risk.
FX swap transactions (CNY/foreign currency) for short-term cash-flow hedging only, approved by the bank treasury desk and documented as treasury liquidity hedges.

Cross-currency swaps are permissible only when matched to an approved foreign-currency debt/financing arrangement with completed SAFE/Foreign Debt registration; no speculative cross-currency swap positions are allowed for the WFOE.

Offshore NDFs are not permissible onshore for the WFOE; the foreign parent may execute NDF-only hedges outside China to manage the RMB/USD exposure arising from the WFOE distributions, but any payments to settle NDFs must be arm's-length and tax-documented.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Credit Information Report to the State Administration for Market Regulation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from January 1 through June 30 covering the previous fiscal year; the first annual report is due in the second calendar year after registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing immediately places the WFOE on the enterprise list with abnormal operations. If the annual report is not remedied within 3 consecutive years, SAMR can list the company as seriously illegal or untrustworthy, publish the violation, impose fines of RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000, and ultimately revoke or strike off the registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Income Tax Annual Settlement Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) and the competent local tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 of the calendar year following the December 31 fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a late-filing penalty of RMB 50 to RMB 2,000 and daily late-payment interest of 0.05% on the tax payable. Under-reported tax can be penalized at 50% to 5 times the underpaid amount; continued refusal can trigger account seizure, dividend export restrictions, legal representative travel bans and ultimately administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Information Report (Foreign Investor and Actual Controller Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and SAMR through the Foreign Investment Comprehensive Reporting System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from January 1 through June 30 for the prior year; shareholding or beneficial ownership changes must be filed within 30 days of the occurrence.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file constitutes a breach of the Foreign Investment Law; authorities may order rectification, impose administrative fines of RMB 20,000 to RMB 50,000 for late filings and up to RMB 100,000 for misrepresentation, and invoke enterprise abnormal list measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership / Actual Controller Annual Confirmation and 30-Day Change Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAMR via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System; beneficial ownership files are subject to PBOC supervisory inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation must be included in the June 30 annual report; any transfer of shareholding or change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be reported to SAMR and the tax authority within 30 days after the corporate registration change is effective.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unlawful delay or omission is subject to rectification orders and administrative fines under the beneficial ownership information measures; willful concealment may lead to fines, public credit downgrade, and inability to complete future capital or equity transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Register Audit and Corporate Records Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors and corporate secretarial records; inspection evidence retained for SAMR and tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Performed concurrently with annual report preparation between January 1 and June 30; updated entries for share transfers must be recorded before the 30-day filing clock begins.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or missing entries in the register of members, directors, charges, or minutes are treated as inaccurate corporate information; SAMR may impose fines of RMB 10,000 to RMB 30,000, and directors may bear civil liability if inaccurate registers prejudice creditors or shareholders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Audit Report of Financial Statements and Shareholder Approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed PRC CPA firm; audited report retained for SAMR, tax, and foreign investment reporting evidence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The audit must be completed and the financial statements approved by the shareholders before June 30; for efficient annual reporting the audit report should be ready by April 30 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Submission of unaudited financial information in the SAMR annual report constitutes false information; the WFOE may be placed on the abnormal list, fined RMB 10,000 to RMB 30,000, and denied tax preferential items or foreign exchange payment benefits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Indirect Tax Reconciliation and Filing (VAT, stamp duty, and local surcharges)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local tax bureau under the State Taxation Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly VAT returns are due by the 15th day after each period; the final annual indirect-tax reconciliation is closed together with the Enterprise Income Tax annual settlement by May 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Each missed VAT return attracts a RMB 50 to RMB 2,000 procedural fine and daily late-payment interest at 0.05%; persistent delinquency may trigger block on invoice quota, on-site tax inspection, understatement penalties of 50% to 5 times the tax amount, and enforcement sales of assets to settle tax arrears.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The legal trigger is the WFOE status itself: PRC law requires every wholly foreign-owned limited liability enterprise to obtain an annual independent CPA audit regardless of balance sheet size, turnover, or headcount. Additional quantitative thresholds apply for full public disclosure and PRC CAS application: for software/console publishing (ISIC 5820), medium enterprises have 100 or more employees and annual operating revenue of RMB 10 million or more; large enterprises have 300 or more employees and annual operating revenue of RMB 100 million or more. Small/micro enterprises may adopt the simplified Small Enterprise Accounting Standards but are still not exempt from the statutory WFOE audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Enterprise (CAS, substantially converged with IFRS) for medium and large enterprises; Small Enterprise Accounting Standards for qualified small/micro entities; audit engagements are performed in accordance with PRC CPA Audit Standards (China Standards on Auditing).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must confirm beneficial ownership and actual controller information in the SAMR annual report every year by June 30. Any shareholding transfer or change in ultimate beneficial ownership requires a 30-day reporting window: the change is first recorded in the corporate registers and passed by shareholder resolution, then filed with SAMR and MOFCOM within 30 days of the effective registration date, and simultaneously disclosed in the annual foreign investment information report for the year in which the change occurs.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - 1,800 per year for registered address plus Chinese corporate secretarial/agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800 - 3,200 per year for a digital-games WFOE with Steam and PlayStation payouts; lower end for simple single-entity operations and higher end where consolidated schedules or transfer pricing documentation are required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small low-profit enterprises (annual taxable income ≤ RMB 3 million, employees ≤ 300, total assets ≤ RMB 50 million) benefit from a reduced effective rate of 5% on taxable income up to RMB 3 million through 2027. High-tech enterprises (with valid High/New Technology Enterprise certificate) are subject to a 15% reduced rate. New integrated circuit enterprises and certain software enterprises may qualify for a two-year exemption followed by a three-year 50% reduction (i.e., 12.5% effective rate). A super-deduction of 100% applies to eligible R&D expenses (200% gross deduction).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Annual Return (Form A05007, '中华人民共和国企业所得税年度纳税申报表') filed via the E-Tax platform (电子税务局) / Xiamen or relevant State Taxation Administration online portal; quarterly prepayment via Form A01051.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly prepayment returns are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter. Annual return and final settlement are due within 5 months (by May 31) after the end of the tax year; if the fiscal year is the calendar year, the annual return is due by May 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Line 1: 营业收入 (Operating Revenue)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenue from sales of goods or services, including video game sales, in-game microtransactions, and platform royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross revenue on accrual basis in RMB. Sales through Steam and PlayStation Store are recognized on a net basis only if a valid agency agreement exists; otherwise record gross platform settlements. All foreign-currency-denominated revenue must be translated at the monthly-average exchange rate published by the People's Bank of China. Adjust for intercompany revenue from your overseas affiliate if the transaction is classified as related-party.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Line 2: 营业成本 (Operating Costs)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to generating revenue, including game development salaries, third-party middleware royalties, server hosting, and platform distribution fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Costs paid to non-resident affiliates must be supported by contractual documents, service records, and proof of actual render. Any management or technical service fees to offshore parent must satisfy the transfer pricing arm's-length standard; disallowed costs include unrelated personal expenses and excessive royalty payments not approved by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Line 3: 税金及附加 (Taxes and Surcharges)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Domestic taxes other than CIT: urban maintenance and construction tax (7% of VAT paid in urban areas), education surcharge (3%), local education surcharge (2%), stamp duty, and property tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No withholding tax on these domestic surcharges. Cross-border payments are subject to VAT and any applicable WHT; input VAT on offshore service imports may be creditable only if a contract, invoice, and proof of service receipt are documented. Ensure stamp duty is paid on cross-border game licensing contracts at the prescribed rates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Line 4: 销售费用 (Selling Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing, user acquisition, platform commissions, store-feature fees, and promotional costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to Steam or PlayStation Store for distribution/promotion must be distinguished from royalty payments. Platform commissions are generally deductible if they are not embedded royalties and are supported by commercial invoices. Related-party marketing fees must be benchmarked under TP rules; excessive fees without commensurate benefit will be adjusted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Line 5: 管理费用 (Administrative Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General corporate overhead: salaries, rent, legal, accounting, and management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocation of offshore group headquarter costs (shared services) must follow a documented cost allocation method and satisfy State Administration of Taxation (SAT) requirements. A service fee to the overseas parent must be supported by detailed timesheets, service agreements, and proof of benefit. Expense without corresponding economic benefit is non-deductible and subject to TP adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Line 6: 财务费用 (Finance Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest expense, foreign exchange losses, and bank charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to a non-resident related lender is subject to 10% WHT unless reduced under a DTA. Deductibility is limited by the thin capitalization rule: net interest on related-party debt exceeding 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio (for non-financial enterprises) is not deductible. Interest must be at arm's-length rates; requiring a loan agreement, SAFE registration if cross-border, and TRC for treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / Line 7: 营业利润 (Operating Profit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue minus cost-of-sales, taxes, operating and financing expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Operating profit must be economically realistic. A WFOE performing development and publishing for overseas affiliates should not report a chronic loss if it bears significant risks and assets, as this will attract TP audits. Recharacterization risk arises when profits are diverted to offshore entities without adequate remuneration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / Line 8: 加：营业外收入 (Add: Non-Operating Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Extraordinary income such as government grants, fines reversals, or insurance settlements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Government software development grants may be taxable unless expressly treated as taxable-free under SAT rules. Any subsidy received as a result of corporate residency must be declared in the year realized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 / Line 9: 减：营业外支出 (Less: Non-Operating Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Extraordinary expenses such as penalties, charitable contributions, or asset write-offs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fines and administrative penalties are non-deductible. Charitable donations are deductible only up to 12% of annual accounting profit and must be made through qualified charitable organizations with valid donation receipts. Cross-border donations to overseas non-profits are generally not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 / Line 10: 利润总额 (Total Accounting Profit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is book profit per Chinese Accounting Standards (CAS). Any discrepancy between this and tax-basis profit must be reconciled in Schedule A105000. For a WFOE with overseas parent transactions, ensure profit not distorted by transfer mispricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 / Line 11: 纳税调整后所得 (Taxable Income after Adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit plus/minus tax adjustments (e.g., disallowed expenses, tax-exempt income, additional deduction for R&D).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Major upward adjustments include non-deductible related-party fees exceeding arm's-length amounts, thin-capitalization interest, and non-deductible entertainment expenses. Downward adjustments include R&D super-deduction (100% of qualifying R&D expenses), software enterprise tax preferences, and losses incurred in overseas branches under DTA non-discrimination provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 / Line 12: 弥补以前年度亏损 (Loss Deduction Carryforward)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of prior-year tax losses within the 5-year carryforward period used to offset current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: WFOE losses can be carried forward 5 years. Cross-border loss offsetting is generally denied: losses of an overseas branch cannot offset domestic profits except in limited DTA-creditable situations. Loss after a change-of-business or capital restructuring may be scrutinized under anti-loss-trafficking rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 13 / Line 13: 应纳税所得额 (Taxable Income Base)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final amount subject to CIT at the statutory or preferential rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE qualifies for High/New Technology Enterprise rate, fill the reduced rate line. Base erosion and anti-abuse rules apply: outbound payments to affiliated entities in no-tax or low-tax jurisdictions may be recharacterized if lacking substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 14 / Line 14: 税率 (Applicable Tax Rate)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 25% standard rate or applicable preferential rate (15% HNTE, 20% small-low-profit adjusted).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Incorrect rate use, especially claiming HNTE without valid CNIPA-recognized certificate, creates underpayment liability and fraud penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 15 / Line 15: 应纳所得税额 (Calculated CIT)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by applicable rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For small low-profit enterprises, calculate the 5% effective rate (i.e., 25% of taxable income after 20% reduction). Non-resident WFOE shareholders do not include this CIT in their home-country return until formally distributed as dividend.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: RMB 2,000 for general returns, up to RMB 10,000 for serious cases; daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of taxes due from the statutory deadline. Understatement due to negligence: 50% to five times the underpaid tax. Willful tax evasion via fraudulent filings (e.g., inflating platform costs or concealing Steam revenue): criminal liability under PRC Criminal Law Art. 201, with imprisonment up to 7 years for especially large amounts. Additional 0.5–monthly fine for failures to keep TP documentation; SAT may also make assessed adjustments and impose a 5% late fee per month on TP adjustments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The outbound dividend WHT rate is 10% under the PRC CIT Law Art. 3 and 37 for non-resident recipients. To claim a reduced rate under a Double Tax Agreement/Arrangement (e.g., Hong Kong DTA under Art. 10, Singapore DTA, US-China treaty Art. 10 at 10% or lower), the recipient must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority for the calendar year containing the dividend payment date; (2) complete the 'Qualifying Person and Beneficial Owner Declaration' in the e-Tax system (e.g., Form F100 for treaty benefits); (3) prove direct or indirect ownership of at least 25% of the Chinese entity if claiming the 5% direct-investment treaty rate (e.g., under HK-CN DTA) for the 365-day holding period; (4) demonstrate beneficial ownership by showing substantive business operations, not conduit/letter-box status, per SAT Announcement 2018 No. 9 (anti-abuse rules); and (5) file the application before remittance, supported by board dividend resolution, audited financial statements, and proof of underlying CIT paid. The Chinese payer withholds the treaty rate at source; a refund procedure is available if excess WHT is withheld but the reduced treaty rate should be applied at the time of distribution if pre-approval obtained. Failure to substantiate beneficial ownership results in denial of treaty benefit and reversion to 10% + potential penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on interest is 10% (CIT Law Art. 3/37) plus 6% VAT (fully deductible part of CIT via formula). Under most DTAs, interest treaty rate is 10% (e.g., US-China 10%, Singapore-China 10%, HK-CN 7% only if associated enterprises conditions) but may be reduced to 0% for interest paid to government financial institutions under some treaties; the Hong Kong-China Arrangement allows 7% WHT for interest paid to qualified HK financial institutions or recognized government body. Royalties for IP (software licensing, game middleware, Steam/console SDK use) are subject to 10% statutory WHT; treaty relief often reduces to 5% or 10% depending on the treaty (e.g., US-China 10%/5% for 'scientific equipment' royalties; Hong Kong-China 7% if beneficial owner is HK company and IP is used in China; Singapore-China 5% for royalties if equipment use qualifies). Royalty WHT is levied on gross payments. VAT on royalties is 6% (deductible for CIT WHT). The payer must withhold both CIT and VAT within 15 days after the obligation arises; non-withholding results in a surcharge equal to 0.5% per month on the unpaid tax up to 50% of the tax due, plus additional CIT liability for the payer if it fails to withhold.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: An annual intercompany related-party transaction amount exceeding RMB 200 million for total related-party revenue/assets/outbound payments (or RMB 20 million for financial assets/equity transfers) triggers mandatory preparation of a Master File; a Local File must be prepared when intercompany controlled transactions in a single category exceed RMB 40 million, or when the entity's related-party transactions exceed RMB 100 million. For video game publishing, any intercompany royalty/service arrangement of any size must still be documented reasonably under the arm's-length principle; SAT may require special adjustments even below thresholds if overall profit indicators look distorted.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: For a Chinese WFOE, the Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as known in offshore centers do not apply domestically, but China applies the substance-over-form doctrine embedded in SAT Announcement No. 9 of 2018 (anti-treaty-shopping), General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR) under CIT Law Art. 120/47, and the 2022 OECD BEPS implementation practices. The WFOE must demonstrate that it performs functions (game development, local publishing, store management), owns assets (IP, contracts, equipment), and bears risks (market risk, credit risk, IP infringement risk) commensurate with its reported profit. If the WFOE merely executes risk-free routine functions while all IP income flows to an offshore low-tax affiliate, SAT may recharacterize the arrangement under the 'corresponding adjustment' and 'substance requirement' principles. The Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) concept, through DEMPE functions (Development, Enhancement, Maintenance, Protection, and Exploitation) is used to attribute profit on embedded intangibles; for Steam/PlayStation publishing, storefront contracts, user data, marketing, and payment settlement activities performed in China are CIGA and require an arm's-length reward. Additionally, China issued Circular 5 of 2021 on TP administration for digital platforms: platform commissions and online-game related-party remuneration must be aligned with value creation and commercial substance; pure cost-plus remuneration for a Chinese developer/reseller is insufficient if the WFOE performs exploitation functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion via Falsified Revenue or Expense Records (Tax Evasion)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully under-reporting digital game sales by routing Steam/PlayStation Store proceeds directly to an offshore parent or shell entity without recording revenue in the WFOE, or fabricating fake platform payout fees and inflated marketing deductions to artificially reduce taxable profit, causing non-payment of CIT and VAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Tax Administration Law (TAL) Art. 63: payment of tax underpaid plus a penalty of 50% to 5 times the underpaid tax; TAL Art. 64: restoration of records and penalty up to RMB 50,000 for failure to file; late surcharge of 0.05% per day on unpaid tax. Criminal liability: PRC Criminal Law Art. 201 (tax evasion) imposes up to 3 years' imprisonment for evasion between RMB 100,000 and 1,000,000, and 3–7 years for evasion above RMB 1,000,000 (or where proportion to tax due is high).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced under PRC Company Law Art. 20 (now Art. 23 under the 2023 revisions) if a director's control of the WFOE causes asset commingling, unjust profit diversion, or evasion of taxes, leading to unlimited personal liability for corporate tax debts. Directors involved in arranging false invoices or fraudulent refunds can be held jointly liable under TAL Art. 57 and subject to personal asset freezing; in serious cases, a criminal conviction under Art. 201 leads to direct imprisonment; the tax authority may also blacklist the director under the 'Joint Disciplinary Action on Tax Payment Integrity' list, with restrictions on high-consumption travel, plane/train travel, property purchases, and exit from China.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Substance Failure and Anti-Avoidance Recharacterization (GAAR / Beneficial Ownership Abusive Scheme)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming a Chinese WFOE as a tax-driven shell or conduit that holds no actual game development/publishing staff, bears no meaningful business risk, and transfers all valuable intangible rights to a tax-heaven affiliate (e.g., Hong Kong, Cayman) solely to claim treaty benefits on dividends/royalties while lacking commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under PRC CIT Law Art. 47 and Art. 120, SAT may apply GAAR to recharacterize the arrangement, deny treaty benefits, and impose adjusted tax plus interest and penalty (TAL Art. 63/64). Announcement 2018 No. 9 denies beneficial-owner status for conduit companies, reverting treaty WHT rates (e.g., from 5% or 0% to 10%). Failure to maintain substance may expose the entity to revocation of the softer (5%) dividends rate and, if fraudulent paperwork filed, criminal liability under Art. 205 (forged VAT invoices) or Art. 201 (evasion).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute a sham substance arrangement face several personal exposures: (a) Personal civil liability for the company's under-withheld taxes under TAL Art. 43 (Responsibility of persons directly in charge), (b) blacklisting as a seriously illegal taxpayer that may lead to travel bans and denial of exit permits, (c) criminal liability under Art. 201 for evasion-organizing and under Art. 229 (Criminal Art. 229 in securities?) for false audits, and in extreme cases; (d) the People's Court may pierce the veil and hold the director personally liable for 100% of unpaid tax and penalty if the company is created as mere instrument of fraud. Imprisonment terms range from 3–7 years for major fraud, with additional fines equal to 50–100% of evaded amount.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Cross-Border Illegal Remittance and Forex / Export Tax Violation (Foreign Exchange and Trade Misreporting)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving overseas Steam/PlayStation payouts directly into an offshore bank account of the parent or director without proper SAFE foreign-exchange registration, while declaring zero or reduced royalties/service fees to Chinese tax authorities; or artificially moving funds out via false 'technical services' contracts and unreported offshore payments, constituting illegal capital flight or evasion of WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC FX Administration Regulations: unauthorized cross-border fund flow may be treated as illegal purchase/sale of foreign exchange under SAFE, subject to fines from 0.5% to 1.5 times the transaction amount (SAFE Art. 6/15, 2008 Regulations). For intentional false export/import declarations, Customs and SAT may apply Administrative Penalty under Customs Law for up to 3 times evaded tax; if the practice is laundering funds, AML Law of PRC Art. 63 imposes fines up to RMB 5 million; Criminal Law Art. 191 (money laundering) imposes imprisonment up to 10 years (severe persons) and fines. If sales are booked as 'software export' with inflated refunds, SAT will claw back VAT export rebates and impose a penalty of 1–5 times the fraudulently obtained export refund plus potential criminal liability for fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who maintain overseas bank accounts in their own name without declaration are personally liable under SAFE's reporting regime; failing to declare foreign-held bank accounts or move RMB proceeds abroad without approval may trigger an administrative fine. Civil liability arises for misappropriation of corporate funds: Company Law Art. 147/148 imposes restitution to the company for any personal gains from undisclosed offshore deposits. In criminal cases, directors who orchestrate fake cross-border service contracts for capital flight may be imprisoned up to 10 years under Art. 191 (money laundering) if the proceeds originate from identified crimes, or up to 5 years for obstructing tax collection. Additionally, the SAT/SAFE blacklisting mechanism prohibits directors from leaving China and blocks their domestic personal bank accounts until the tax and penalty are settled.
